'''Claudia de Rham''' (born 29 March 1978) is a Swiss [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] working at the interface of gravity, cosmology, and particle physics. She is based at [[Imperial College London]]. She was one of the UK finalists in the Physical Sciences and Engineering category of the [[Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists#Past United Kingdom (UK) Laureates and Finalists|Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists]] in 2018 for revitalizing the theory of [[massive gravity]] and won the award in 2020.

==Early life and education==
De Rham was born in [[Lausanne]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.epflalumni.ch/the-alumni-awards/|title=Alumni Award Recipients|website=www.epflalumni.ch|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> She completed her undergraduate studies in France, receiving a ''[[Diplôme d'Ingénieur]]'' in physics at the [[École Polytechnique]] in Paris in 2000.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://blavatnikawards.org/honorees/profile/claudia-de-rham/|title=Claudia de Rham {{!}} Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|website=blavatnikawards.org|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> She received a master's degree in physics from the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] in 2001.<ref name=":1" /> In 2002, de Rham moved to the UK, achieving a PhD in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Cambridge]] on "[[braneworld]] cosmology beyond the low-energy limit".<ref>{{Cite book|last=Claudia|first=De Rham|date=2005|title=Braneworld cosmology beyond the low-energy limit}}</ref> She has trained as a pilot and made it through several stages of the [[European Astronaut Corps|European Space Agency's astronaut selection process]].<ref name="devlin" />

==Research==
After earning her PhD, de Rham went to Montreal to join the physics department at [[McGill University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.physics.mcgill.ca/seminars/CHEP_de-rham.html|title=McGill Physics: CHEP seminars|website=www.physics.mcgill.ca|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.physics.mcgill.ca/chep/reports/chep_20072008_seminars_all.html|title=CHEP Seminars 2007–2008|website=www.physics.mcgill.ca|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> She moved to [[McMaster University]] in Hamilton and the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in Waterloo, Ontario, in 2006, where she worked in a joint postdoctoral position in cosmology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/people/claudia-de-rham|title=Claudia de Rham {{!}} Perimeter Institute|website=www.perimeterinstitute.ca|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> In 2010, she joined the [[University of Geneva]] as an assistant professor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/personal/crham/Jobs.html|title=Claudia de Rham|website=www.perimeterinstitute.ca|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cosmology.unige.ch/users/claudia-de-rham|title=Claudia de Rham {{!}} Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics – University of Geneva|website=cosmology.unige.ch|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> She moved to [[Case Western Reserve University]] in Cleveland, Ohio, in 2011 and became an associate professor there in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.phys.cwru.edu/~claudia/|title=Claudia de Rham|website=www.phys.cwru.edu|access-date=17 January 2018|archive-date=16 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170416044839/http://www.phys.cwru.edu/~claudia/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://origins.case.edu/ted/|title=TED {{!}} Institute for the Science of Origins|website=origins.case.edu|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> She joined [[Imperial College London]] in 2016. That year, she was awarded a £100,000 Wolfson Merit Award from the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/naturalsciences/physics/newssummary/news_24-3-2017-15-10-7|title=Expanding horizons: throwing new light on dark energy|last=|first=|date=|website=Imperial College London|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170402220850/http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/naturalsciences/physics/newssummary/news_24-3-2017-15-10-7|archive-date=2 April 2017|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/claudia-de-rham-12796/|title=Claudia de Rham|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref>

Her research is in the area of [[Physical cosmology|theoretical cosmology]], and she explores gravitational models that could explain the accelerated expansion of the universe. De Rham is recognised as a researcher at the forefront of the development of theories of [[massive gravity]], where the particle carrier of the gravitational force, the [[graviton]], may be massive.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.tedxcle.com/claudia-de-rham/|title=Claudia de Rham {{!}} TEDxCLE|website=www.tedxcle.com|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> In 2010, she constructed a nonlinear{{Clarify|date=May 2024|reason=It isn't clear what the word "nonlinear" means in this context.}} theory of a massive graviton, which is theoretically consistent and [[Ghost (physics)|ghost]]-free.<ref name="resummation">{{Cite journal|last1=de Rham|first1=Claudia|last2=Gabadadze|first2=Gregory|last3=Tolley|first3=Andrew J.|date=2011|title=Resummation of Massive Gravity|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=106|issue=23|article-number=231101|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.106.231101|pmid=21770493|arxiv=1011.1232|bibcode=2011PhRvL.106w1101D|s2cid=3564069}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rham|first=Claudia de|date=1 December 2014|title=Massive Gravity|journal=Living Reviews in Relativity|language=en|volume=17|issue=1|page=7|doi=10.12942/lrr-2014-7|doi-access=free |pmid=28179850|pmc=5256007|issn=2367-3613|arxiv=1401.4173|bibcode=2014LRR....17....7D}}</ref> That formulation of massive gravity is now known as "de Rham-Gabadadze-Tolley (dRGT) theory", owing to its discovery by de Rham, [[Gregory Gabadadze]], and Andrew J. Tolley.<ref name="resummation" /> Her research helps tackle the problem of the [[cosmological constant]] and could describe the accelerated expansion of the universe as a purely gravitational effect, where massive gravitons are responsible for [[dark energy]].<ref name=":1" />

In 2015, she gave a [[TED (conference)#TEDx|TEDx]] talk titled "Nature of the Graviton".<ref name=":3" /> She gives regular public lectures about theoretical cosmology.<ref>{{Cite De Rham was interviewed by [[Morgan Freeman]] in season 8 of ''[[Through the Wormhole]]''.<ref name="m124">{{cite web | title=Professor Claudia de Rham | website=Imperial College London | date=1 April 2024 | url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/physics/engage-with-us/outreach/fundamental-physics/claudia/ | access-date=8 October 2024}}</ref>

==Publications==
In November 2023, de Rham co-authored ''The Encyclopedia of Cosmology, Set 2: Frontiers in Cosmology, [https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/13578-vol1?fbclid=IwAR1gB0XAm5XIq5xQudEZKQdp1E_Lg_aTxNH-xASofgumzCHGIvtfvgCbQDs#t=aboutBook Volume 1: Modified Gravity]'', with Andrew J Tolley, also of Imperial College London.<ref name="a740">{{cite book | last=Rham | first=Claudia de | last2=Tolley | first2=Andrew J. | title=Encyclopedia of Cosmology, the – Set 2: Frontiers in Cosmology (in 3 Volumes) | publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company | publication-place=Hackensack | date=22 November 2023 | isbn=978-981-12-8969-9}}</ref> In April 2024, she published ''The Beauty of Falling: A Life in Pursuit of Gravity''.<ref>{{cite book | last=Rham | first=Claudia de | title= The Beauty of Falling: A Life in Pursuit of Gravity | publisher=Princeton University Press | publication-place=Princeton, New Jersey  | date= 2 April 2024 | isbn=978-0-691-23748-0}}</ref>

==Awards and leadership roles==
* 2010–2014: PI on Swiss National Foundation Professorship Grant, for the project "Challenging the cosmological paradigm"<ref name=":4" />
* 2012–2013: PI on ACES Advance Opportunity Grant, for the project "Recent Developments in Massive Gravity"<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/c.de-rham|title=Home – Claudia de Rham|website=www.imperial.ac.uk|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref>
* 2016–2021: Royal Society Wolfson Merit Award<ref name=":2" />
* 2017: [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] Alumni Award<ref name=":0" />
* 2017–2021: PI on [[Simons Foundation]] Award, "Origins of the Universe" program with [[Rachel Rosen]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2017/07/21/new-initiative-ponders-origins-of-the-universe/|title=New Initiative Ponders Origins of the Universe {{!}} Simons Foundation|website=Simons Foundation|access-date=17 January 2018|date=21 July 2017}}</ref>
* 2017–2022: PI on ERC consolidator grant, for the project "Massive Gravity and Cosmology"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/newssummary/news_25-4-2017-17-26-52|title=Multi-million EU funding boost for Imperial researchers|last=Scheuber|first=Andrew|date=|website=Imperial College London|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425010101/http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/newssummary/news_25%2D4%2D2017%2D17%2D26%2D52|archive-date=25 April 2017|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref>
* 2018: [[St John's College, Cambridge]] [[Adams Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2017-18/weekly/6505/section3.shtml|title=Awards, etc. – Cambridge University Reporter 6505|website=www.admin.cam.ac.uk|access-date=25 May 2018}}</ref>
* 2018: [[Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists]]: finalist, UK Physical Sciences and Engineering<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sciexaminer.com/news/science/theoretical-physicist-gets-awarded-2018-blavatnik-awards-3500.html|title=Theoretical physicist gets awarded in the 2018 Blavatnik Awards|date=16 January 2018|work=Science Examiner|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/newssummary/news_12-1-2018-15-23-33|title=Imperial physicist wins first-of-its-kind science prize|last=Dunning|first=Hayley|date=|website=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116010101/http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/newssummary/news_12%2D1%2D2018%2D15%2D23%2D33|archive-date=16 January 2018|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref>
* 2020: Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists: winner, UK Physical Sciences and Engineering<ref name="blavatnik2020">{{cite web |title=Three innovative scientists receive US$100,000 (£75,000) each from prestigious Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|url=http://blavatnikawards.org/news/items/three-innovative-scientists-receive-us100000-75000-each-prestigious-blavatnik-awards-young-scientists/ |website=Blavatnik Awards Young Scientists |publisher=New York Academy of Sciences |access-date= 18 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="devlin">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2020/jan/25/has-physicists-gravity-theory-solved-impossible-dark-energy-riddle |title=Has physicist's gravity theory solved 'impossible' dark energy riddle? |work=[[The Guardian]] |last=Devlin |first=Hannah |author-link=Hannah Devlin |date=25 January 2020 |access-date=25 January 2020}}</ref>
* 2023: Elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2023|title=New members|year=2023|publisher= American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=21 April 2023}}</ref>
